paper.title: The on-line shortest path problem under partial monitoring

settings.name_in_paper: On-line shortest path problem in the multi-armed bandit setting (edge losses on chosen path revealed)
unmapped: Actions are u-v paths in a known directed acyclic graph; path loss is sum of edge losses in [0,1], so path losses lie in [0, K_path]
All paths assumed to have equal length K_path (achievable by graph augmentation)
Algorithm uses a covering set of paths C and knows |E|, N, K_path
settings.definition_quote: at each time instance $t=1,\ldots,n$, the decision maker picks a path $\bI_t \in \cP$ from $u$ to $v$. Then the environment assigns loss $\ell_{e,t} \in [0,1]$ to each edge $e \in E$, and the decision maker suffers loss $\ell_{\bI_t,t}=\sum_{e \in \bI_t} \ell_{e,t}$. In the unrestricted case the losses $\ell_{e,t}$ are revealed for all $e \in \bI_t$ ... Note that in both cases $\ell_{e,t}$ may depend on $\bI_1,\ldots,\bI_{t-1}$

settings.name_in_paper: Combination of the label efficient and bandit settings for shortest paths
unmapped: Label efficient: edge losses on chosen path observed only upon request; queries made with probability eps_q each round (total queries bounded by m with high probability for appropriate eps_q)
Actions are u-v paths in a DAG, all of equal length K_path; edge losses in [0,1]
settings.definition_quote: This means that the decision maker only has access to the loss of the chosen path upon request and the total number of requests must be bounded by a constant $m$.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit tracking of the shortest path (competing with time-varying paths with m switches)
unmapped: Actions are u-v paths in a DAG, all of equal length K_path; edge losses in [0,1]
Comparator: best m-partition (sequence of paths with m switches)
settings.definition_quote: The goal of the decision maker is to perform as well as the best time-varying path (partition), that is, to keep the normalized regret $\frac{1}{n}\left(\wh{L}_n-\min_{\bt,\ui} L(\P(n,m,\bt,\ui))\right)$ as small as possible (with high probability) for all possible outcome sequences.

settings.name_in_paper: Restricted multi-armed bandit problem for shortest path (only total path loss observed)
unmapped: Actions are u-v paths in a DAG (paths need not have equal length; K_path is longest path length); edge losses in [0,1]
Algorithm uses a 2-barycentric spanner basis of b paths
settings.definition_quote: the forecaster has access to the sum $\ell_{\bI_t,t}$ of losses over the chosen path $\bI_t$ but not to the losses $\{\ell_{e,t}\}_{e\in\bI_t}$ of the edges belonging to $\bI_t$.
